A: Only one representative enqueue edge (API -> queue); Web/Auth publishing and worker->Postgres access are not shown
Telemetry dashed lines start 4px off the zone borders (float slightly) and the right telemetry rail is visually busy
Connector labels at 10.5px are at the edge of legibility at half size, though the paint-order halo keeps them readable
B: Zone subtitle text in pastel tints (#60a5fa, #a78bfa, #34d399 on tinted bands) is roughly 2:1 contrast and effectively disappears at half size
No role="img" or aria-labelledby; title/desc only, so weaker accessibility markup
Fixed width/height attributes: opening the file in a smaller window clips with scrollbars instead of scaling (A, viewBox-only, scales)
Shared reads/writes bus erases which service uses which store; only Auth visually publishes jobs (documented, but the drawing alone misleads)
Hand-placed magic coordinates and repeated card/icon markup with no defs reuse beyond markers/filter; costlier to edit

notes: Both are complete (all 11 components, three zones, labelled connectors, legends, valid XML, unique IDs, resolving refs) and both render without collisions at full size. A wins on rendered quality and rigor: zero crossings on a strict column grid, measured contrast with halo-backed labels that survive half size, full a11y markup, and a defs/symbol system that makes it maintainable. B is attractive and tells a good protocol story on its edge labels, but its pastel subtitles fail at half size, it clips rather than scales when opened small, and its data bus trades correctness of specific service-to-store relationships for tidiness.
